target_customer: Engineering, support and product teams at software companies, and AI coding agents needing codebase context
problem: Teams struggle to understand large business critical codebases, which slows documentation, support investigation and onboarding.
business_model: Enterprise software sold through contact sales

founders.name: Adam Tilton
education: University of Illinois Urbana-Champaign, BS, MS and PhD (ABD) in mechanical engineering, computer science, control
founders.background_notes: Role from the PR Newswire launch release; one directory lists titles reversed.

founders.name: Daniel Hensley
education: UC Berkeley, PhD 2017, Magnetic Particle Imaging

investors: more than a dozen angels and early stage investors

technical_complexity.rationale: Computing accurate, symbol complete context over very large legacy codebases with LLMs needed indexing and verification work beyond a simple wrapper.

defensibility.rationale: Enterprise deployment into customer repos and workflows creates some lock in, but code search and AI coding vendors work on adjacent problems.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Coding assistants expanded codebase context features; Driver repositioned toward context for AI agents and support investigation by 2026.

market_need_then: Large legacy codebases and fast LLM progress created demand for automated documentation; launch customer UICO said Driver helped it understand systems and port software.

branding.domain_note: Company uses driver.ai and driverai.com; USPTO filings by Driver AI, Inc. in Austin, with DRIVER DOCS as a key brand per a trademark directory.

identity.voice_and_tone: Enterprise and plain: software understanding for everyone who needs it

brand_strength.rationale: Generic word and confusable with the unrelated Drive.ai, no brand press found.

pivots.to: context layer for codebases and AI agents plus support investigation
pivots.why: The site and YC description now describe context for agents; the exact date is not stated, so 2025 is approximate.

outcome_analysis: Driver launched out of stealth in October 2024 with an $8M seed led by GV and by 2026 names Optiver, Geneva Trading, ShipBob and Lucanet as customers. Serial founders with two earlier exits and enterprise traction explain the seed, while a pivot toward agent context shows it adapting to coding agents. No later round or exit was found.
